questions.stem: What is rebound pain after regional anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Acute postoperative pain once effective regional anaesthesia wears off, as surgical pain is unmasked

questions.stem: How common is rebound pain after regional anaesthesia?
After which kind of regional technique is rebound pain most common?
questions.answer: Techniques that give complete analgesia and surgical anaesthesia

questions.stem: Which patients are at higher risk of rebound pain after regional anaesthesia?
options: Older men having soft tissue surgery
Bony surgery, preoperative pain or opioid use, young women

questions.stem: What does the evidence show about hyperalgesia as a cause of rebound pain?
questions.answer: Little evidence that hyperalgesia causes it

questions.stem: What can be done before surgery to help prevent rebound pain?
questions.answer: Warn patients what to expect as the block wears off and surgical pain starts

questions.stem: What analgesic strategy is recommended to prevent rebound pain?
Which non-drug measure can help prevent rebound pain after regional anaesthesia?
For selected patients, what can help prevent rebound pain beyond single-shot blocks?
What role do perineural adjuncts play in prolonging single-shot blocks?
What are possible harms of perineural adjuncts?
questions.answer: Drug errors from mixing, longer motor block, side effects, neurotoxicity

questions.stem: By which routes can dexamethasone be given as a block adjunct?
options: Subcutaneously only, as a skin wheal

questions.stem: At about what perineural dexamethasone dose is there a ceiling effect?
How does perineural dexmedetomidine act on the nerve?
options: Activates alpha-2 receptors on peripheral axons
Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis in the nerve
Blocks HCN channels, which restore resting potential
Stimulates potassium efflux to deepen the membrane

questions.stem: Why does perineural dexmedetomidine not depend on alpha-2 receptors?
questions.answer: Peripheral nerve axons lack alpha-2 receptors
